intl.title: Ferris State - Apply as an International Student

sch.title: Ferris State - Incoming International Student Scholarships

test_policy.notes: The CDS (C8) says Ferris is test optional and considers ACT/SAT scores if submitted. The international page says SAT is not required and can substitute for English scores. A SAT or ACT score is one input to the Woodbridge N. Ferris scholarship amount (the top Founder's tier needs ACT 31/SAT 1350).

requirements.notes: Apply online and choose 'International - All Levels'. Needs official secondary transcripts and finishing exams (the office converts them to a U.S.-equivalent GPA used for admission and scholarships), English proof, a financial statement of $36,600 in liquid funds (the 'Canadian students' figure is lower), and a passport copy. Decision and scholarship come within 2 weeks of a complete file; the $100 International Orientation fee is paid after admission to receive the I-20. BS in Artificial Intelligence and BS in Information Security and Intelligence require an essay; College of Engineering Technology programs require proven math proficiency. The application fee is not stated on the pages read.

deadlines.label: Application (fall 2027): no international undergraduate deadline published
deadlines.notes: The international undergraduate page lists no deadline; decisions come within 2 weeks of a complete file. Confirm with the Office of International Education and allow time for the I-20 and visa.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Other proofs: SAT reading/writing 510+, ACT reading 19+, ELS level 112 with C or better, IB English 4+, A-level C or higher, CEFR B2, IGCSE/O-level/GCSE grades in English, or two or more years at a U.S. high school, an IB school, or an English-medium international school, or a semester of credit at a U.S. college. Citizens of listed English-speaking countries may be exempt. Ferris may require an English placement test on arrival.

english.notes: New TOEFL iBT scoring system (1-6 scale).

cost.notes: International page: estimated first-year international tuition $24,416 per year (14 credits per semester at $872 per credit; the page does not state the academic year). Housing, meal plan and health insurance about $15,336 per year. CDS G1 (2026-27, final July 2026): on-campus food and housing $12,035 for first-year students. Canadian students pay in-state tuition (about $14,952).

aid.notes: Woodbridge N. Ferris Scholarships are automatic for first-time international students, based on high school GPA (4.0 scale) plus a submitted test score: Founder's up to $10,000/yr (3.9 GPA and ACT 31/SAT 1350/TOEFL 96/IELTS 7.5/PTE 66/Duolingo 120), President's $6,500 (4.0), Provost's $5,500 (3.5), Dean's $4,500 (3.25-3.49), Ferris Crimson $3,000 (3.0), each renewable at 2.75-3.3 cumulative GPA. The international page says awards of $3,000 to $10,000 are made at admission. Students can earn up to $15,000 a year in an on-campus job. CDS H6: 68 nonresident undergraduates received institutional aid averaging $12,130. No need-based aid for international students is described.
